name: Child-to-Parent Domain Escalation (krbtgt SID-History OR Trust Key)
description: Escalate from child domain to parent forest root by forging a golden ticket with the parent's Enterprise Admins SID (S-1-5-21-<parent>-519) in SID History.

steps.label: Forge golden ticket with EA SID in history

examples.label: Forge golden ticket with EA SID history

recommended.note: Forest trust abuse for external forests

notes: EA SID = S-1-5-21-<parent_domain>-519. Added to SID History field. PAC validation accepts child-signed tickets via transitive trust. | Two lab methods: (LO19) child krbtgt -> golden ticket with parent EA SID in SID History (steps above); (LO18) dump the child<->parent trust key (lsadump::trust /patch) -> forge a referral TGT with /service:krbtgt /target:<parent> -> asktgs for a parent service (variations). Intra-forest trusts do NOT SID-filter by default, so the EA SID is honored.

defense.why_it_works: In an AD forest, the Enterprise Admins and Schema Admins groups live in the forest root domain. When an attacker controls a child domain (via its krbtgt hash), they can forge a TGT with SID History containing the SID of the parent domain's Enterprise Admins group (S-1-5-21-<parent-SID>-519). The inter-realm TGT includes the extra SID - when the KDC in the parent domain processes the referral ticket, it honors the SID History (if SID filtering is not enforced between parent/child in the same forest, which is the default) and grants EA-level access.
defense.prerequisites: Compromised child domain krbtgt hash. Child domain SID and parent domain SID. Enterprise Admins SID (S-1-5-21-<parent-domain-SID>-519). Rubeus /golden with /sids parameter or Mimikatz kerberos::golden /sids. Network access between child and parent.
defense.impact: T1134.005 Access Token Manipulation: SID-History Injection + T1558.001 Golden Ticket. Escalates from child domain DA to forest root Enterprise Admin. Full forest compromise - all domains affected. Only 2 krbtgt rotations in the child domain + 2 in the forest root can remediate.
defense.detection:
Event 4769 in the parent domain: TGS request with an inter-realm TGT containing extra SIDs from the child domain. MDI: 'Suspected cross-domain privilege escalation' / 'Inter-realm ticket with extra SIDs'. The inter-realm TGT contains SID History entries not present in the actual user's AD attributes - requires PAC inspection to detect.
Suspicious token manipulation chains: token-related APIs (LogonUser, DuplicateTokenEx) or runas commands → new process spawned under different security context (e.g., SYSTEM) → mismatched parent-child process lineage or ETW token/PPID anomalies → abnormal lateral movement or privilege escalation activity (DET0283/AN0786).
defense.artifacts: MDI alert: inter-realm privilege escalation | Parent DC Event 4769: inter-realm TGT referral with extra SIDs | Child DC Event 4769: cross-domain referral ticket issued | SIEM: authentication from child domain user accessing forest root resources with EA-equivalent rights
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4769
| where like(Account_Domain, "%child%") AND Service_Name!="krbtgt"
| table _time, Account_Name, Account_Domain, Service_Name, Client_Address, Ticket_Encryption_Type

index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4768
| where Ticket_Encryption_Type="0x17" AND Account_Domain!="<parent_domain>"
| table _time, Account_Name, Account_Domain, Client_Address
defense.elastic_kql:
event.code:"4769" AND winlog.event_data.TicketOptions:*0x40810000* AND source.domain:*child*

event.code:"4768" AND winlog.event_data.TicketEncryptionType:"0x17"
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4769
| where TargetDomainName != "<domain>"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, ServiceName, TargetDomainName, IpAddress
| join kind=leftouter (IdentityDirectoryEvents | where ActionType has "SID History") on $left.TargetUserName == $right.AccountName
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
defense.prevention:
Enable SID filtering between parent and child domains: netdom trust ChildDomain /domain:ParentDomain /enablesidhistory:no. PAC validation at forest root. MDI deployment. Rotate krbtgt in both domains after a compromise. Treat child domain compromise as a full forest compromise for response purposes.
Privileged Account Management: Limit permissions so users/groups cannot create tokens (GPO: Computer Configuration > Security Settings > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment: Create a token object = local system only; Replace a process level token = local and network service only). Admins should log in as standard user and use runas for elevated tasks.
User Account Management: Restrict users to least privileges; adversary must already have administrator-level access to fully exploit token manipulation.
defense.evasion: Use AES256 for the forged inter-realm TGT. Only add the minimum EA SIDs needed. Access parent domain resources via legitimate services to blend inter-realm traffic.
defense.misconfiguration: SID filtering not enforced between parent and child domains (default within a forest - by design). No MDI deployment. krbtgt passwords stale in child domains (attackers work down the trust chain systematically).
defense.vulnerable_config:
# SID filtering typically NOT applied within a forest (by design):
Get-ADTrust -Filter {Target -eq 'CHILD.CORP.LOCAL'} | Select-Object SIDFilteringForestAware,SIDFilteringQuarantined
# SIDFilteringForestAware: False, SIDFilteringQuarantined: False
# → SID History in tickets crosses the trust = child DA → Forest EA

# Required: child domain krbtgt hash (from child domain compromise):
# Then: Rubeus /golden /user:DA /domain:child.corp.local /sid:<child-SID> /sids:<parent-EA-SID> /rc4:<krbtgt-hash>
defense.secure_config:
# Enable SID filtering on parent-child trust (breaks SID History but hardens forest):
netdom trust CHILD.CORP.LOCAL /domain:CORP.LOCAL /enablesidhistory:no /filtersids:yes

# Or use Selective Authentication on forest trust:
Set-ADTrust CHILD.CORP.LOCAL -SelectiveAuthentication $true

# Deploy MDI on ALL DCs including child domain DCs:
# MDI cross-domain correlation detects privilege escalation across trust boundaries

# Treat child domain compromise as forest compromise:
# Incident response: rotate krbtgt in BOTH child and parent domains
# + change all DA passwords in both domains

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Windows Security Event Log for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Check for credential dumping artifacts (LSASS access, SAM hive reads, Kerberos anomalies)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

variations.label: Alt method (LO18): dump inter-realm TRUST KEY
variations.command: Invoke-Mimikatz -Command '"lsadump::trust /patch"'   # note the [In] key for the parent domain

variations.label: Forge referral TGT with the trust key + parent EA SID
Request a parent-domain TGS with the forged ticket
DCSync parent forest root after escalation

explain:
Forges a cross-domain golden ticket that escalates from a child domain to the forest root:
  golden                    forge a TGT offline
  /rc4:<nt_hash>            the child domain's krbtgt hash (from DCSync)
  /domain:<domain> /sid:<domain_sid>   the child domain and its SID
  /sids:<parent_enterprise_admin_sid>  the parent Enterprise Admins SID (ends -519) injected into SID History
  /user:Administrator /ptt  impersonate Administrator and inject the ticket
SID History is not filtered inside a forest, so the ticket is honored on the parent DC - dir \\<parent_dc>\C$ then DCSync the root.
